text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Army commander says he supports criticism of Islamist-led government by an army officer.
- Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan plans to develop the impoverished southeast, which has been hit hard by a 12-year-old fight between the army and rebel Kurds.
- Opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz says the ruling Islamist-conservative coalition will collapse soon.
- Islamist MP calls media organisations "devils" for attacking the government.
- Political tension will rise ahead of a key meeting of top military and government figures at the weekend.
- An Islamist council in Istanbul tried to end the lease of a private hospital for employing males in the maternity wards.
- Istanbul industrialists are looking to invest in other parts of Turkey, including the impoverished east.
